title: Ardashir and Hayat al-Nufus

full_text:
Prince Ardashir, son of King Bilqis of Shiraz, was a youth of peerless beauty, martial skill, and poetic learning. Hearing of Princess Hayat al-Nufus, daughter of the King of the White Isle, who had secluded herself in a remote garden fortress and vowed never to marry, Ardashir resolved to win her heart through subtlety and respect.

Accompanied by an elderly, wise merchant, Ardashir sailed to the White Isle. Instead of approaching with armed ships, he opened an exquisite art pavilion in the capital, displaying magnificent paintings and rare illustrated manuscripts.

Knowing that Princess Hayat al-Nufus visited the public gardens on Fridays, Ardashir painted a breathtaking fresco upon the pavilion wall: a garden of white lilies surrounded by crystal streams, where a noble falcon guarded a gentle dove from a desert serpent.

When the princess saw the painting, she was moved by the delicate allegorical message: that true courtship is not a cage of tyranny, but a sanctuary of protection and mutual freedom.

She initiated a poetic correspondence with the anonymous artist. For months, they exchanged verses of philosophical depth, testing each other’s minds, until their mutual admiration blossomed into pure love.

When Ardashir revealed his royal identity before her father’s court, Princess Hayat al-Nufus joyfully consented to wed him, celebrating a union founded on intellectual equality, artistic refinement, and enduring respect.
moral: Patience, literary nobility, and respectful courtship conquer the most guarded heart.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
